scope: Proposition 2.2 (Exponentially decaying representative) of the manuscript “The ℓ¹-Bass Conjecture for Discrete Groups” (preprints/The-l1-Bass-Conjecture-for-Discrete-Groups-October-5-2026/l1-bass-conjecture.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 207 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 9894680d2ffb10ff), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 4. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let e ∈ Mq(ℓ1(G)) satisfy e2 = e. There are a finitely generated subgroup Γ ≤ G, a word length | · | on Γ, a number c > 0, and an idempotent p ∈ Mq(ℓ1(Γ)) such that X h∈Γ |p(h)|1ec|h| < ∞, (2.1) and p is similar to e in Mq(ℓ1(G)). If the trace of every such p has finite support on finite-order conjugacy classes of Γ, the same conclusion holds for every e over every discrete group.
